claim_boundary: This packet covers the Sequential Impulse row of DART's cross-solver-matched, publication-shaped Figure 13 reconstruction and links the same-host AVBD/VBD comparison packet. Together they establish three DART solver variants on one reconstructed scene, not three source-equivalent published rows. The packet does not reproduce XPBD, claim exact unpublished source-scene constants, establish CUDA parity, or compare against a published/source timing.

semantic_review.claim_and_expected_observation: This review covers only DART's publication-shaped 252-brick Sequential Impulse reconstruction: the three impact regions should fracture locally at frame 14, followed by large-scale constraint drift and wall collapse by frame 120.
semantic_review.not_proven_and_limitations: These images do not establish the paper's unpublished source constants, scale, geometry, or material model; they do not prove the XPBD row, CUDA parity, published or source timing parity, matched-accuracy performance, or full cross-solver paper parity.
semantic_review.reconciliation_and_verdict: PASS for the bounded DART reconstruction only: both engine ViewReports pass framing and visibility checks; the frame-14 numeric oracle identifies five broken joints confined across all three impact regions; the frame-120 oracle records unchanged fracture identity, severe retained-row residuals, and collapse thresholds passing; the inspected images show an initially standing wall and a later wall lying nearly flat. This is not a pass for source-scene or full paper parity.
semantic_review.reviewer_capability: native image input at original 1280x720 detail
semantic_review.text_oracle: The runtime-resolved public_sequential-impulse scene reports five broken joints distributed 2, 1, and 2 across the three impact regions with all initial-fracture checks passing at frame 14; at frame 120 it reports 19.0 percent total retention, 27.3 percent outside retention, large residuals, and all configured collapse checks passing.
semantic_review.visible_observation: At frame 14 the wall remains upright while the balls occupy the three impact locations and local brick offsets are visible. At frame 120 the wall has rotated or folded down into an almost horizontal sheet while the balls rest in front of it. The reconstruction is visibly much smaller and simpler than paper Figure 13.
